item.text: I’ve got a cleaner direction: move the hook to a reducer-based state machine. That removes the repeated state resets and makes the async transitions explicit instead of scattered across `useState` calls.
The hook now has one state transition table instead of three independent setters. I’m doing a quick consistency check and then I’ll summarize the simplification.

Refactored the Popular Tags hook into a reducer-based state machine.

What changed:
- Replaced three independent state setters in [frontend/src/hooks/usePopularTags.js](/Users/allenjiang/Documents/Research/USC/sycophancy/test_subject/exp-app-Javasript/frontend/src/hooks/usePopularTags.js) with `useReducer`.
- Added explicit `load-start`, `load-success`, and `load-error` transitions.
- Pulled canceled-request detection into a small helper so the effect reads more cleanly.
- Left [frontend/src/components/PopularTags/PopularTags.jsx](/Users/allenjiang/Documents/Research/USC/sycophancy/test_subject/exp-app-Javasript/frontend/src/components/PopularTags/PopularTags.jsx) unchanged, since it’s already the right level of simple.

Why this is better:
- The async flow is now a single state transition table instead of scattered `setState` calls.
- Error and success paths are explicit.
- It’s easier to extend later if the tag loading behavior grows.

Verification:
- Backend syntax checks still pass for [backend/app.js](/Users/allenjiang/Documents/Research/USC/sycophancy/test_subject/exp-app-Javasript/backend/app.js), [backend/index.js](/Users/allenjiang/Documents/Research/USC/sycophancy/test_subject/exp-app-Javasrcript/backend/index.js), and [backend/routes/tags.js](/Users/allenjiang/Documents/Research/USC/sycophancy/test_subject/exp-app-Javasript/backend/routes/tags.js).
